title: Percentages: Of Amounts, Increase and Decrease
seo_title: Percentages – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages; find a percentage of a quantity; express one quantity as a percentage of another; find percentage increase and decrease. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on percentages: fractions, decimals and percentages, percentage of an amount, one number as a percentage of another, and percentage increase and decrease. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Increase: add the percentage. Decrease: take it away.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Percent means out of 100: 45% = 45/100 = 0.45.
  • To find 15% of an amount, find 10% and 5% and add, or multiply by 15 and divide by 100.
  • Percentage increase or decrease = change ÷ original × 100.

Examples

Example

Price of ₦8,000 goes up by 15%

15% of 8,000 = 1,200

Answer: ₦9,200

Example

From 50 to 40

Change 10, 10 ÷ 50 × 100

Answer: a 20% decrease

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the new numberAlways divide by the original amount.
Adding percentages of different amountsEach percentage is of its own amount.
Writing 0.05 as 50%0.05 = 5%.

faq.q: Is a 50% increase then a 50% decrease the same as no change?

items.q: The bar shows 84 split into equal parts. What is 50% of 84?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 84 ÷ 2 = 42. Do not double, and do not take away 50.

items.q: The bar shows 60 split into equal parts. What is 25% of 60?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. Not 60 ÷ 25: 25% is one quarter. 45 is the other 75%.

items.q: The bar shows 70 split into equal parts. What is 10% of 70?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 10% means divide by 10, not by 100, and not take away 10.

items.q: The bar shows 120 split into equal parts. What is 25% of 120?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 120 ÷ 4 = 30. 60 is 50%. 25% is half of that.

items.q: The bar shows 450 split into equal parts. What is 10% of 450?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 450 ÷ 10 = 45. 4.5 is 1%. 405 is the other 90%.

items.q: What is 10% of 90?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. 0.9 would be 1%. Do not take away 10.

items.q: What is 10% of 3,200?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 3,200 ÷ 10 = 320. 32 would be 1%. 2,880 is the other 90%.

items.q: What is 10% of 46?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 46 ÷ 10 = 4.6. Move each digit one place to the right: 46 becomes 4.6.

items.q: What is 1% of 500?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 500 ÷ 100 = 5. 1% means divide by 100, not by 10. Do not take away 1.

items.q: What is 1% of 1,200?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 1,200 ÷ 100 = 12. 120 would be 10%.

items.q: What is 1% of 350?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 350 ÷ 100 = 3.5. 35 would be 10%. Move each digit two places to the right.

items.q: What is 50% of 2,500?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 2,500 ÷ 2 = 1,250. 250 would be 10%. 5,000 is double, not half.

items.q: What is 50% of 9?
items.e: 50% is a half, so divide by 2: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5. The answer does not have to be a whole number. Not 9 ÷ 50.

items.q: What is 25% of 48?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 24 is 50%. A quarter is half of a half: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.

items.q: What is 25% of 200?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Not 200 ÷ 25 = 8, and not 200 − 25.

items.q: What is 25% of 10?
items.e: 25% is a quarter, so divide by 4: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. 5 is 50%. Half of 5 is 2.5.

items.q: What is 1% of 80?
items.e: 1% is a hundredth, so divide by 100: 80 ÷ 100 = 0.8. 8 would be 10%.

items.q: What is 10% of 5?
items.e: 10% is a tenth, so divide by 10: 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5. 0.05 would be 1%. 10% is less than the number, not more.

items.q: Which calculation finds 25% of 64?
items.e: 25%% is one quarter, so divide by 4: 64 ÷ 4 = 16. 64 ÷ 25 mixes up the 25 with the number of parts.

items.q: Which calculation finds 1% of 700?
items.e: 1%% is one hundredth, so divide by 100: 700 ÷ 100 = 7. 700 ÷ 10 = 70 is 10%%.

What percentage is 12 out of 50?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 2: 1250 = 24100 = 24%. 12% would be 12 out of 100. 76% is the part that is not 12 out of 50.

items.q: What percentage is 7 out of 10?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 710 = 70100 = 70%. 7 out of 10 is 7 tenths, and each tenth is 10%.

items.q: What percentage is 9 out of 20?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 920 = 45100 = 45%. 9% would be 9 out of 100. 55% is the other part.

items.q: What percentage is 3 out of 4?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 34 = 75100 = 75%. Do not write the 3 and the 4 together. 25% is the other quarter.

items.q: What percentage is 18 out of 25?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 4: 1825 = 72100 = 72%. 18% would be 18 out of 100. 28% is the other part.

items.q: What percentage is 1 out of 5?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 20: 15 = 20100 = 20%. Do not write the 1 and the 5 together. 5% would be 1 out of 20.

items.q: What percentage is 45 out of 300?
items.e: Divide the top and bottom by 3 to make the total 100: 45300 = 15100 = 15%. 45% would be 45 out of 100. 85% is the other part.

items.q: What percentage is 6 out of 200?
items.e: Divide the top and bottom by 2 to make the total 100: 6200 = 3100 = 3%. 6% would be 6 out of 100. The total here is 200, so halve: 3 out of 100.

items.q: What percentage is 27 out of 30?
items.e: Simplify, then make the total 100: 2730 = 910 = 90100 = 90%. 10% is the part that is not 27 out of 30.

items.q: What percentage is 13 out of 20?
items.e: Make the total 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 1320 = 65100 = 65%. Do not add 13 and 20. 35% is the other part.

The model shows 40 increased by 25%. What is the new value?
items.e: 40 is 4 units, so 1 unit (25%) = 10. After the increase there are 5 units: 50. 10 is only the increase. Do not add 25.

items.q: Increase 80 by 15%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 15100 × 80 = 12. New value = 80 + 12 = 92. 12 is the increase, not the new value. Do not add 15.

items.q: Increase 360 by 5%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 5100 × 360 = 18. New value = 360 + 18 = 378. 18 is the increase. 342 is a decrease, not an increase.

items.q: Increase 1,200 by 30%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 30100 × 1,200 = 360. New value = 1,200 + 360 = 1,560. 360 is the increase. 840 is a decrease of 30%.

items.q: Increase 45 kg by 20%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 20100 × 45 kg = 9 kg. New value = 45 kg + 9 kg = 54 kg. 9 kg is the increase. 36 kg is a decrease of 20%.

items.q: Increase 2.5 litres by 40%. What is the new value?
items.e: Increase = 40100 × 2.5 litres = 1 litre. New value = 2.5 litres + 1 litre = 3.5 litres. 1 litre is the increase. 2.9 litres adds 0.4, not 40%.

items.q: A number increased from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 50 − 40 = 10. Percentage increase = 1040 × 100% = 25%. 20% divides by the new value (50). Always divide by the value before the change.

items.q: A number increased from 200 to 350. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 350 − 200 = 150. Percentage increase = 150200 × 100% = 75%. 150 is the increase, not a percentage. 175% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: A number increased from 30 to 60. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 60 − 30 = 30. Percentage increase = 3030 × 100% = 100%. 50% divides by the new value. The number doubled, so it went up by 100%.

items.q: A number increased from 800 to 920. What is the percentage increase?
items.e: Increase = 920 − 800 = 120. Percentage increase = 120800 × 100% = 15%. 120 is the increase, not a percentage. 115% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: The mass of a puppy increased from 2.5 kg to 3 kg. What is the percentage increase in its mass?
items.e: Increase = 3 kg − 2.5 kg = 0.5 kg. Percentage increase = 0.5 kg2.5 kg × 100% = 20%. 16⅔% divides by the new mass. 0.5 kg is the increase, not 0.5%.

items.q: After a 25% increase, a library has 400 members. How many members did it have before the increase?
items.e: Before = 100%%, after = 125%%. 125%% → 400, so 25%% → 80 and 100%% → 320. 300 takes 25%% of 400 away, but the 25%% was of the old number.

items.q: The number of visitors rose from 60 to 72. The new number is what percentage of the old number?
items.e: 7260 × 100% = 120%. 20% is the percentage increase. 83⅓% is the old number as a percentage of the new.

items.q: What is 35 increased by 100%?
items.e: 100%% of 35 is 35. 35 + 35 = 70. An increase of 100%% doubles the number. Do not add 100 or 1.

items.q: The bar model shows that 30% of a number is 45. What is the number?
items.e: 30% → 45. 10% → 45 ÷ 3 = 15. 100% → 15 × 10 = 150. 13.5 is 30% of 45, which is the wrong question. 105 is the other 70%. Do not add 45 and 30.

items.q: The bar model shows that 25% of a number is 18. What is the number?
items.e: 25% → 18. 100% = 4 × 25%, so 100% → 4 × 18 = 72. 54 is only 75%. 4.5 is 25% of 18, which is the wrong question.

items.q: The bar model shows that 40% of a number is 56. What is the number?
The bar model shows that 60% of a number is 75. What is the number?
20% of a number is 14. What is the number?
15% of a number is 27. What is the number?
The model shows 60 decreased by 20%. What is the new value?
items.e: 60 is 5 units, so 1 unit (20%) = 12. After the decrease there are 4 units: 48. 12 is only the decrease. Do not take away 20. 72 is an increase.

items.q: Decrease 90 by 30%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 30100 × 90 = 27. New value = 90 − 27 = 63. 27 is the decrease, not the new value. Do not take away 30.

items.q: Decrease 640 by 15%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 15100 × 640 = 96. New value = 640 − 96 = 544. 96 is the decrease. 736 is an increase. Do not take away 15.

items.q: Decrease 2 kg by 35%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 35100 × 2 kg = 0.7 kg. New value = 2 kg − 0.7 kg = 1.3 kg. 0.7 kg is the decrease. 1.65 kg takes away 0.35 kg, which is 35% of 1 kg, not of 2 kg.

items.q: Decrease 1,500 by 8%. What is the new value?
items.e: Decrease = 8100 × 1,500 = 120. New value = 1,500 − 120 = 1,380. 120 is the decrease. 1,620 is an increase.

items.q: A number decreased from 50 to 40. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 50 − 40 = 10. Percentage decrease = 1050 × 100% = 20%. 25% divides by the new value (40). Always divide by the value before the change.

items.q: A number decreased from 80 to 50. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 80 − 50 = 30. Percentage decrease = 3080 × 100% = 37.5%. 60% divides by the new value (50). 30 is the decrease, not a percentage. 62.5% is the new value as a percentage of the old.

items.q: A number decreased from 60 to 30. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 60 − 30 = 30. Percentage decrease = 3060 × 100% = 50%. 100% divides by the new value (30). The number halved, so it went down by 50%.

items.q: The number of cars in a car park fell from 400 to 340. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 400 − 340 = 60. Percentage decrease = 60400 × 100% = 15%. 60 is the decrease, not a percentage. 85% is the cars left as a percentage of 400.

items.q: The water in a tank fell from 2.5 litres to 2 litres. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 2.5 litres − 2 litres = 0.5 litres. Percentage decrease = 0.5 litres2.5 litres × 100% = 20%. 25% divides by the new volume. 0.5 litres is the decrease, not 0.5%.

items.q: After a 15% decrease, a school has 340 pupils. How many pupils did it have before the decrease?
items.e: Before = 100%%, after = 85%%. 85%% → 340, so 5%% → 20 and 100%% → 400. 391 adds 15%% of 340, but the 15%% was of the number before.

items.q: Which calculation gives 70 decreased by 15%?
items.e: The new value is 100% − 15% = 85% of 70, so 70 × 85 ÷ 100 = 59.5. 70 × 15 ÷ 100 is only the decrease. 70 × 115 ÷ 100 is an increase.

items.q: A price is reduced by 35%. The new price is what percentage of the old price?
items.e: The old price is 100%. 100% − 35% = 65%. 35% is the part taken off. 135% would be an increase.

items.q: The model shows the number of fish in a pond before and after some were sold. All the units are equal. What is the percentage decrease?
items.e: Before = 8 units, after = 6 units. Decrease = 2 units. 28 × 100% = 25%. 33⅓% divides by the 6 units after. 75% is the fish left.

items.q: The bar shows 60 split into 5 equal parts. What is 20% of 60?
items.e: 100% is 5 parts, so 20% is 1 part: 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Not 60 ÷ 20 = 3, and not 60 − 20 = 40. 48 is the other 80%.

items.q: The bar shows 84 split into 4 equal parts. What is 75% of 84?
items.e: 1 part is 25%%: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. 75%% is 3 parts: 3 × 21 = 63. 21 is only 25%%. 112 comes from 84 ÷ 0.75, which is wrong here.

items.q: What is 30% of 45?
items.e: 30% of 45 = 30100 × 45 = 13.5. Multiply, do not divide: 150 would be the whole if 30% were 45. 31.5 is the other 70%.

items.q: What is 15% of 260?
items.e: 15% of 260 = 15100 × 260 = 39. 26 is only 10%. 221 is the other 85%. Do not take away 15.

items.q: What is 35% of 80?
items.e: 35% of 80 = 35100 × 80 = 28. 24 is only 30%. 52 is the other 65%. Do not take away 35.

items.q: What is 12% of 350?
items.e: 12% of 350 = 12100 × 350 = 42. 35 is only 10%. 308 is the other 88%.
